A phantom pair is one business, and has no need to share the work between its two names. Different schemes leave different traces, which is why we use many screens.
    :::

5.  **Different weights.** The audit team decides that a register link and identical BOQ rates should each count as 2, because they point directly to contact between bidders. Recompute the scores with these weights, and see whether the order of the groups changes.

    ::: {.callout-tip collapse="true"}
    ## Solution
    ```{r}
    ex_scores <- map(list(c("F03", "F07", "F11"), c("F17", "F18"), c("F08", "F24"),
                          c("F21", "F23", "F25"), c("F13", "F16"), c("F02", "F12")),
                     group_screens) |>
      list_rbind() |>
      mutate(score = (closed_share >= 0.5) + coalesce(margin_sd <= 1.5, FALSE) +
               coalesce(inside_gap >= 3, FALSE) + (win_ratio >= 0.97) +
               2 * register_link + 2 * identical_rates) |>
      arrange(desc(score)) |>
      select(group, score)
    ex_scores
    ```
    With the new weights, the Bhimganj group scores `r ex_scores$score[ex_scores$group == "F03 F07 F11"]`, `F17` and `F18` score `r ex_scores$score[ex_scores$group == "F17 F18"]`, and `F08` and `F24` score `r ex_scores$score[ex_scores$group == "F08 F24"]`. No comparison group scores more than `r max(ex_scores$score[!ex_scores$group %in% c("F03 F07 F11", "F17 F18", "F08 F24")])`. The phantom pair has caught up with the ring. The weights changed how the suspects compare with each other, which is why they must be fixed and justified before the scores are seen.
    :::

6.  **A lower bar for losers.** Rerun Screen 9 on firms with at least 20 bids and a win share below 0.3, using `firm_record`. For each firm, find the standard deviation of its margin above the firm that beat it most often. Which firm has the steadiest margin?

    ::: {.callout-tip collapse="true"}
    ## Solution
    ```{r}
    ex_lose <- firm_record |>
      filter(bids >= 20, win_share < 0.3)

    ex_losses <- bids |>
      filter(firm %in% ex_lose$firm, !winner) |>
      left_join(bids |>
                  filter(winner) |>
                  select(tender_id, beaten_by = firm, win_pct = quoted_pct),
                by = "tender_id") |>
      mutate(margin = quoted_pct - win_pct)

    ex_rival <- ex_losses |>
      count(firm, beaten_by, sort = TRUE) |>
      slice(1, .by = firm)

    ex_steady <- ex_losses |>
      semi_join(ex_rival, by = c("firm", "beaten_by")) |>
      summarise(main_rival = first(beaten_by), losses = n(),
                sd_margin = round(sd(margin), 2), .by = firm) |>
      arrange(sd_margin)
    ex_steady
    ```
    `r nrow(ex_lose)` firms now pass, against `r nrow(always_lose)` in the chapter. `F18` still has the steadiest margin, `r ex_steady$sd_margin[ex_steady$firm == "F18"]`, against `F17`. Next come `F25` and `F23`, both of Devnagar and both beaten most often by `F16`, at `r ex_steady$sd_margin[ex_steady$firm == "F25"]` and `r ex_steady$sd_margin[ex_steady$firm == "F23"]`. Two Devnagar firms losing to the same rival by fairly steady margins fits the reading of Screen 6, that a quiet arrangement held prices up before the newcomer came. It is a lead to check against the dates, not a finding.
    :::

## Summary of functions used

| Function | Package | What it does |
|-----------------------|----------------|--------------------------------|
| `count()`, `summarise(.by = )` | dplyr | Counts bids, wins and tenders by firm, district and year |
| `pivot_wider()`, `pivot_longer()` | tidyr | Turns year counts into columns, and the register into one row per detail |
| `inner_join(relationship = "many-to-many")` | dplyr | Joins a table to itself to find pairs of firms in the same tender, the same register detail or the same BOQ rate |
| `separate_longer_delim()` | tidyr | Splits the list of directors into one row each |
| `paste(sort(), collapse = )` | base R | Builds the line-up of bidders in a tender |
| `pmin()`, `pmax()` | base R | Puts the two firms of a pair in a fixed order |
| `sample()`, `replicate()` | base R | Shuffles the order of wins many times, for the reshuffling test |
| `pbinom()` | stats | Chance of so few repeats under the binomial distribution |
| `sd()`, `mean()`, `median()` | stats, base R | Margin steadiness, mean bids and median ratios |
| `t.test()` | stats | Compares the mean ratio before and after the newcomer |
| `slice(.by = )`, `semi_join()` | dplyr | Keeps each firm's most frequent rival, and only the losses to that rival |
| `map()`, `list_rbind()` | purrr | Applies the screens to every candidate group and stacks the results |
| `geom_histogram()`, `geom_point()`, `geom_vline()` | ggplot2 | Plots the cover margins and the Devnagar ratios over time |
